title: Familiars
summary: Spirit companions bound to a mage as partners, not servants.

claims.text: Familiars bond with mages on a magickal level, trading knowledge and abilities for upkeep, company and Quintessence; they are in no way the mage's servants.

title: Dupes and slaves of the Nephandi
summary: The mortal tools of the Fallen.

claims.text: Nephandi prefer to steer Sleeper groups such as Satanists, neo-Nazis, the Klan, some secret societies and even some Masonic lodges, without open meddling.
Hidden guides inside these groups slowly corrupt them toward Nephandic ends; dupes who ask too many questions vanish and become slaves.

title: Servants of the Marauders
summary: Mortals drawn into a Marauder's madness.

claims.text: Spear-carriers, often dreamers and lovers of art or games, take bit parts in a Marauder's world until they believe in it; some fight as shock troops on the Gauntlet.
Jesters are Sleepers who know of the Ascension War and work to make openings for the Marauders.
A Marauder has a familiar only if the Marauder's paradigm calls for one, and such familiars tend to be wildly outrageous or blend into the Marauder's Quiet.

title: The Crossovers
summary: A worldwide, cross-Tradition network of mages' companions.

claims.text: The Crossovers are loosely democratic and reach one another through a facilitator who runs the place they meet, often a bar, coffee house, motel or craft shop with Cross or Over in its name.
Their openness leaves them exposed to Technocratic discovery and infiltration.

title: The Corpselight Connoisseurs
summary: Six Euthanatos consors who fear they have helped commit murder.

claims.text: All six serve Euthanatos mages and have come to suspect that what they were told was the release of spirits was murder.

title: Red Flag
summary: Vigilante companions sworn to end the Ascension War by killing all mages.

claims.text: Every member has lost someone to the Ascension War; they come from Tradition, Technocracy and Marauder circles alike, and hold Nephandi and their servants as prime targets.
Red Flag believes ordinary people will be safe only once mages, werewolves, vampires and all others with supernatural power are gone.
